### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, A40's outgoing transitions split between A14 (about 38 in 100), A15 (about 31) and A20 (about 31); in the later window, all of A40's outgoing transitions go to A21. [DIR006]
- In the earlier window, A14, A15 and A20 each led only to A21; in the later window, A14 leads to A23 (about 52 in 100 transitions) or A27 (about 48), A15 to A23 (about 54) or A27 (about 46), and A20 to A27 (about 61) or A23 (about 39). [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003]
- In the earlier window, A22 always led to A23 and A23 always to A27; in the later window, A22 leads to A23 in about 52 in 100 transitions and to one of A14/A15/A20 in about 48, while A23 leads to A27 in about 48 and to one of A14/A15/A20 in about 52. [DIR004, DIR005]
- The order between the trio A14/A15/A20 and A21/A22 flipped completely: earlier, the trio ran before A21 and A22 whenever they co-occurred (e.g., A14 before A21 in about 38 in 100 traces, never after); in the later window, A21 precedes A14 in about 31 in 100 traces and A14 precedes A21 never, and the same reversal holds for A15 and A20. [REL001, REL002, REL004, REL005, REL006, REL007]
- A14, A15 and A20 now occur about 60% of the way through the trace (mean relative position about 0.59–0.60, versus about 0.31–0.33 earlier), while their participation barely moved (A14 about 38→31 in 100 traces, A15 31→33, A20 32→37, together still about one occurrence per trace); A21, A22 and A23 still appear in every trace, each shifting only about 0.02–0.03 of the trace earlier. [POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, POS006]
- Step gaps moved consistently with this: A40→A21 narrowed from two steps to one in all traces, A22→A27 widened from two steps to three in all traces, and the A22→A23 and A23→A27 gaps, previously fixed at one step, now split between one and two steps (about 52/48 and 48/52 in 100 traces). [LAG001, LAG002, LAG003, LAG004]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that the one-of-three block A14/A15/A20 was moved to a later place in the flow: in the earlier window each trace ran A40, then exactly one of A14/A15/A20, then A21 and later A22, A23 and A27; in the later window A40 leads directly to A21, and the trio executes once after A22, either between A22 and A23 or between A23 and A27, before the trace reaches A27. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, DIR006, REL001, REL003, REL008, LAG001, LAG002, LAG003, LAG004, POS001, POS002, POS003]

The support is direct and consistent: the relational indicator shows the order reversal with A21/A22 directly and completely, the routing changes at A40, the trio, A22 and A23 all point the same way, the trio's position shifts by about 0.27–0.29 of the trace while its total participation stays at one occurrence per trace (fitting a relocation rather than a frequency change), and the gap changes match a one-step insertion around A23. With 24 qualifying items against roughly 0.4 expected if nothing had changed, and empirical strength about 0.995 for every item (differences this large are rare in random re-splits of unchanged data), chance alone explains the overall pattern poorly. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, DIR006, POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, POS006, REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006, REL007, REL008, LAG001, LAG002, LAG003, LAG004]

Limitations: the 24 items largely restate one trace-level pattern rather than independent confirmations, and the trio's routing splits rest on only about 61–76 outgoing transitions per window, so exact shares such as A14's 52/48 split are approximate. An important competing explanation the evidence cannot fully rule out is sampling differences in variant frequencies — a process that always allowed both placements could produce this picture if the earlier window happened to contain only early-placement variants and the later window only late-placement ones, although a complete order reversal across 200 traces per window makes a pure sampling effect unlikely. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, REL001, REL003, POS001, LAG002]
